title: Test and code image analysis · Level 1
slo: Describe how to send an image and text prompt to a deployed Foundry model.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe structured output? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Structured output follows an expected schema or structure. This makes the response predictable.
An organized expected format is part of the definition. Structured output is not merely free-form text.

options.text: It sends an image to a model.
options.rationale: Sending an image provides model input. Structured output concerns the returned result.
options.better_fit: Use this idea when describing a multimodal request.

options.rationale: A deployment name identifies a deployed model. It does not prescribe response format.
options.better_fit: Use a deployment name in MODEL_NAME.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Structured output follows an expected organized structure.

exercises.question_text: What is the Foundry playground used for?

options.rationale: The playground is an interactive environment for testing deployed models. Users can try prompts and uploaded images.

options.text: Calling a deployment from Python code
options.rationale: Python code calls a deployment through an SDK and API configuration. The playground is for interactive testing.
options.better_fit: Use the OpenAI Python SDK for programmatic calls.

options.rationale: Base64 converts image bytes to safe ASCII text. It is not a testing environment.
options.better_fit: Use Base64 for image data embedded in JSON.

options.rationale: A deployment name is an identifier used by code. The playground lets a user test the deployment.
options.better_fit: Use the deployment name in MODEL_NAME.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The playground is for interactive testing.

exercises.question_text: Tool use means a model can invoke designated tools as part of completing a task.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This choice misses an action capability.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Tool use enables invocation of designated tools.

exercises.explanation: Correct. This is the definition of tool use.

exercises.question_text: The Foundry playground is only for writing application code and cannot test uploaded images.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This choice would overlook a useful validation environment.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Users can select a vision-enabled model, attach an image, and test prompts in the playground.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The playground supports interactive image testing.

exercises.question_text: Which items are needed to connect Python code to a Foundry deployment? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The resource key is the API credential used to authenticate. It is a connection setting.
The endpoint is the URL to which requests are sent. The client must use it.
MODEL_NAME must contain the chosen deployment name. This identifies the deployment to call.
Base64 image data may be request content, not a core connection setting. It neither authenticates nor identifies the deployment.
options.better_fit: Use Base64 when an image's binary data must be embedded in JSON.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The connection uses the key, endpoint, and deployment name.

exercises.question_text: Which model family supports text and image inputs for enterprise agent scenarios?

options.rationale: GPT-5 series supports multimodal input for enterprise and agentic scenarios. It is the named model family in the lesson.
This is a broad capability label, not the specific model family requested. It does not identify the GPT-5 series.
options.better_fit: Use this label when generally describing a model that can interpret visual input.

options.rationale: The playground is an interactive testing environment. It is not a model family.
options.better_fit: Use the playground to test a deployed model with prompts and images.

options.rationale: The Responses API is a programmatic interface for requests. It is not a model family.
options.better_fit: Use the Responses API when code must send multimodal inputs.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-5 series is the advanced multimodal family described.

exercises.question_text: The OpenAI Python SDK can call OpenAI-compatible APIs, including Foundry deployments.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would incorrectly rule out the supported Python library.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The OpenAI Python SDK calls OpenAI-compatible APIs, including Foundry.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The SDK can call Foundry deployments.

exercises.question_text: GPT-5 series models accept only text input and cannot reason over images.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This choice would exclude a multimodal model family.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: GPT-5 series can reason across text and image inputs.

exercises.explanation: Correct. GPT-5 series supports text and image inputs.

exercises.question_text: Which facts describe the OpenAI Responses API in Foundry? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The Responses API supports native multimodal inputs, including images. Images can be included with text.

options.text: It is designed for agentic applications.
options.rationale: The API is designed for agentic applications. This is a stated characteristic of the API.

options.text: It is only a portal test screen.
options.rationale: A portal test screen describes the Foundry playground. The Responses API is code-facing.
options.better_fit: Use the Foundry playground for interactive portal testing.

options.text: It is an image encoding method.
options.rationale: Base64 is an image encoding method. The Responses API accepts requests.
options.better_fit: Use Base64 when converting binary image bytes to ASCII text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The Responses API is agentic and supports image input.

exercises.question_text: What does Base64 encoding do for an image?

options.text: Converts binary bytes to safe ASCII text
options.rationale: Base64 converts binary image bytes into safe ASCII text. This makes the data suitable for JSON or URLs.
An endpoint is a URL for sending requests. Base64 changes image data into text.
options.better_fit: Use an endpoint to configure the request destination.

options.rationale: A resource key is an API credential. Base64 is an encoding for image bytes.
options.better_fit: Use a resource key to authenticate a Foundry request.

options.text: Formats model output as a schema
options.rationale: Structured output controls response format. Base64 controls image input representation.
options.better_fit: Use structured output when results must match an expected schema.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Base64 turns image bytes into safe ASCII text.

exercises.question_text: In one Responses API request, the model can process text and image inputs simultaneously.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would incorrectly split inputs that can be sent together.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A single Responses API request can contain text and image input.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The API processes both inputs together.

exercises.question_text: Base64 encoding turns image bytes into an API key for a Foundry resource.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The request would still lack an authentication credential.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A resource key is a credential, while Base64 is image-data encoding.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Base64 encodes bytes; it does not create credentials.

flashcards.back: Model output formatted to an expected organized schema or structure.
It lets a model invoke designated tools during a task.
A web address that supplies image input to a model.
The deployment name chosen for the model.
